newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends stronger in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends stronger in dull trading.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed stronger on Tuesday at 26.375 to the dollar amid sluggish trading, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.377 on Monday.
The Central Bank kept its dollar selling rate at 26.377, setting a floor and warding off speculators.
A total of $179 million were traded, down from Monday's $238.7 million. Done rates ranged from 26.374 and 26.376.
Another trader said the peso's strength was due to the narrowing of the trade deficit.
The country reported a narrowing trade deficit in the first four months of the year to $860 million from $1.319 billion a year ago.
"It has put some confidence back in the market," he said.
Inflows of foreign funds following a rise in Treasury bill rates also partly helped boost the peso.
Traders were expecting the rates to remain steady in the next few days, unless the Central Bank adjusts its dollar selling rate again on Friday.
